questions.stem: A 45-year-old female presents to the clinic with fatigue and weakness. Laboratory tests reveal the following red blood cell parameters: Hemoglobin is 11.2 g/dL, Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) is 103 fL and Red Cell Distribution Width value is 18.5%. the bilirubin levels are normal. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the abnormal red cell parameters in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia

Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to ineffective erythropoiesis, with a mixture of larger-sized (macrocytic) and smaller-sized (normocytic) red blood cells, resulting in an elevated RDW. The macrocytic anemia seen in vitamin B12 deficiency is a characteristic feature and can explain the patient's symptoms of fatigue and weakness.

questions.stem: A young male Shantanu undergoes a routine check-up which reveals he has elevated mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration with slightly reduced MCV. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Hereditary spherocytosis

 

An increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC >34) and increased red cell distribution width (RDW >14%) associated with normal or slightly decreased MCV on an ordinary blood count report should always raise the suspicion of HS.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Iron deficiency anemia: Typically shows low MCHC and low MCV (microcytic, hypochromic anemia).

 

Option B. Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia: Shows increased MCV (macrocytic anemia), not reduced.

 

Option D. Thalassemia minor: Shows low MCV, but MCHC is normal or low, not elevated.

questions.stem: An elderly gentleman Murtaza presents to his family physician with complaints of fatigue. The fatigue has been developing for several months. He also reports being constipated over the past few weeks. He has a family history of colonic adenocarcinoma. Laboratory testing reveals a hemoglobin of 10.2 g/dL and an MCV of 70 fL. The patient is scheduled for a colonoscopy, which reveals a mass in the rectum. A biopsy reveals an invasive adenocarcinoma. Of the following, testing would most likely reveal?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased ferritin, decreased serum iron, decreased TIBC

options.label: B
options.text: Increased ferritin, increased serum iron, increased TIBC

options.label: C
options.text: Decreased ferritin, increased serum iron, decreased TIBC

options.label: D
options.text: Decreased ferritin, decreased serum iron, increased TIBC

questions.answerText: Decreased ferritin, decreased serum iron, increased TIBC
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Decreased ferritin, decreased serum iron, increased TIBC

Decreased ferritin, decreased serum iron, decreased % Tf saturation and increased TIBC are seen with iron deficiency anemia.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old female presents with fatigue, weakness, and tingling sensations in her hands and feet. Physical examination reveals pale skin and glossitis. Laboratory tests show a decreased hemoglobin level and an elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV). Peripheral blood smear reveals hypersegmented neutrophils. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Pernicious anemia

Pernicious anemia is a type of megaloblastic anemia, characterized by vitamin B12 deficiency due to inadequate absorption, typically caused by an autoimmune destruction of parietal cells in the stomach, leading to impaired intrinsic factor production.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old male African immigrant with no significant past medical history is referred to hematology for evaluation of anemia discovered incidentally on routine blood work. A complete blood count shows a leukocyte count of 3500cells/microL and a hemoglobin of 10.1 g/dL. The mean cell hemoglobin concentration is 24 g/dL, and the mean corpuscular volume is 76 fL. His serum ferritin level is 260ng/mL. A hemoglobin electrophoresis test shows elevated HbA2. A peripheral blood smear is likely to show which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Target cells

This patient has β-thalassemia minor. Unlike β-thalassemia major, patients with β-thalassemia minor usually only have a mild hypochromic, microcytic anemia that resembles iron deficiency. A peripheral blood smear would be expected to show some target cells.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the transport molecule involved in iron metabolism marked as “X”?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. Ferroportin

questions.stem: A 65-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with pallor and fatigue. A complete blood count reveals a hemoglobin of 8.2 g/dL. The total bilirubin is 6.4 mg/dL, and direct bilirubin is 0.2 mg/dL. Her lactate dehydrogenase is elevated, and a direct antibody test causes agglutination with anti-IgG. Her peripheral smear reveals spherocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Warm antibody hemolytic anemia

This patient’s laboratory studies are consistent with a hemolytic anemia. The positive direct antibody test indicates an autoantibody as the cause. MC autoimmune hemolytic anemia is warm antibody hemolytic anemia, caused by IgG autoantibodies against red cell antigens (C).

questions.stem: A 20-year-old female presents with the following laboratory values: hemoglobin 9 gm%, MCV is 55fl, RBC is 4.5 million/mm3. There is no history of blood transfusion. What is the most likely diagnosis out of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Thalassemia minor

 

Thalassemia major patient presents with severe anemia and cannot survive without blood transfusion, so this option can be easily ruled out. For other options, Mentzer index is useful for differentiating between thalassemia minor and iron deficiency anemia.

 

Thalassemia minor often presents with mild to moderate anemia and a low MCV. The Mentzer index, calculated as MCV divided by the RBC count, is less than 13 in thalassemia minor.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Thalassemia major: Patients with thalassemia major typically present with severe anemia requiring regular blood transfusions. The degree of anemia in the vignette is not consistent with thalassemia major.

 

Option C. Iron deficiency anemia: Iron deficiency anemia typically presents with microcytic and hypochromic anemia. The Mentzer index is generally greater than 13, which is not the case here.

 

Option D. Anemia of chronic disease: Anemia of chronic disease usually presents with normocytic or sometimes microcytic anemia, but it is often characterized by a normal or increased storage iron level, which can be evaluated by serum ferritin.

 

Educational Objective:

 

When presented with mild to moderate microcytic anemia and an MCV/RBC count that yields a Mentzer index of less than 13, thalassemia minor is a likely diagnosis.

questions.stem: What will be the corrected reticulocyte count in a patient with a hemoglobin of 5 and absolute reticulocyte count of 9%?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D. 3%

questions.stem: A 10 year boy Rohan after playing football complaining fatigue and abdominal pain. He also had a history of hand swelling in past. On ultrasonography, he has shrunken spleen. What is the likely diagnosis of this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Sickle cell anemia (Ref: Robbins 9th/636-7)

Presence of fatigue is likely to be due to anemia. Shrunken spleen is likely to be due to autosplenectomy and swelling of the hand can be attributed to dactylitis or ‘hand foot syndrome’. So, the clinical picture given in the stem of the question is likely to be associated with sickle cell anemia. Shrunken spleen and hand swelling is not seen in other options like iron deficiency anemia, pancreatitis and intermittent porphyria.



Robbins 9th/636-7)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of intravascular hemolysis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. PNH

PNH is a disease that results from acquired mutations in PIGA gene. Red cells deficient in these GPI-linked factors are abnormally susceptible to lysis or injury by complement which manifests as intravascular hemolysis.

questions.stem: Hepcidin inhibits which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Ferroporti

Hepcidin inhibits iron transfer from the enterocyte to plasma by binding to ferroportin and causing it to be endocytosed and degraded.

questions.stemHtml: A 56-year-old female presents in the month of December with chronic fatigue and cyanosis of nose with blue lips. A peripheral blood smear showed the following image. What is the most likely cause of the findings seen?

options.label: A
options.text: Clumps of RBCs due to IgM mediated cold autoimmune haemolytic anemia

options.label: B
options.text: Clumps of RBCs due to IgG mediated warm autoimmune haemolytic anemia

options.label: D
options.text: Clumps of RBCs due to IgG mediated cold autoimmune haemolytic anemia

questions.answerText: Clumps of RBCs due to IgM mediated cold autoimmune haemolytic anemia
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Clumps of RBCs due to IgM mediated cold autoimmune haemolytic anemia

The image shows agglutinated red cells. Since the history mentions that cyanosis is seen affecting fingers and tips of nose in the month of December, it suggests that the red cells agglutinated with cold antibody associated autoimmune haemolytic anemia.

questions.stem: A pathologist is examining the liver biopsy of a 20-year-old male with cirrhosis. A Prussian blue stain reveals extensive positivity. Laboratory testing does not reveal HbH or Hb Barts. Of the following, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. β-thalasssemia major

Individuals with β-thalassemia major require blood transfusions from the time of birth and can easily develop a secondary hemochromatosis, which could lead to cirrhosis of the liver (B). An individual with a significantly decreased production of α chains would have HbH (β tetramers) and HbBart (four γ chains) (A). None of the other diseases is a significant risk factor for cirrhosis (C-E).

questions.stemHtml: A 10-year-old boy Rishi presents with chronic fatigue. Physical examination reveals slight jaundice and splenomegaly. The results of laboratory studies include hemoglobin of 11.8g/dL, hematocrit of 30%, total bilirubin of 2.5 mg/dL, and conjugated bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL. The peripheral blood smear is shown in the image. The osmotic fragility of the patient’s RBCs is increased, but the Coombs test is negative. Defects in which of the following are involved in the pathogenesis of this disorder?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Erythrocyte cytoskeleton

The smear shows many RBCs to be spherocytes, with decreased diameter and no central pallor. Hereditary spherocytosis (HS) represents a heterogeneous group of inherited disorders of the erythrocyte cytoskeleton, characterized by a deficiency of spectrin or other cytoskeletal components (ankyrin, protein 4.2, band 3).

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man from Chhatisgarh presents with increasing fatigue. He has a 3-year history of tuberculosis, and CBC shows a mild microcytic anemia. Blood work-up demonstrates low serum iron, low iron-binding capacity, and increased serum ferritin. The pathogenesis of anemia in this patient is most likely caused by which of the following mechanisms?

options.label: C
options.text: Impaired utilization of iron from storage sites

options.label: D
options.text: Synthesis of structurally abnormal globin chains

questions.answerText: Impaired utilization of iron from storage sites
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Impaired utilization of iron from storage sites

Anemia of chronic disease arises in association with chronic inflammatory diseases (e.g., TB and RA) and malignant conditions. Chronic disease leads to ineffective use of iron from macrophage stores in the bone marrow, resulting in a functional iron deficiency.

questions.stemHtml: A 28-year-old woman delivers a male neonate at 36 weeks of gestation. The mother has a history of poor prenatal care and several previous miscarriages. Examination of the neonate reveals marked pallor and generalized edema (anasarca), and the peripheral blood smear is shown in the image. The nucleated cells in this blood smear are which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Erythroblasts

The peripheral blood smear displays erythroid precursors, which are normally confined to the bone marrow. Hemolytic disease of the newborn is associated with complement-mediated hemolysis of fetal erythrocytes and resulting in the release of numerous erythroid precursors (erythroblasts). The other choices represent normal immune cells.

questions.stem: All of the following can cause reticulocytosis except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Aplastic anemia

Aplastic anemia is associated with reticulocytopenia.

questions.stem: Abnormality in Schilling test can be seen in all of the following except:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B. Folic acid deficiency

questions.stemHtml: A patient with a peripheral smear as given develops multiple splenic infarcts. Which of the following is a common complication of autosplenectomy in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Pneumonia

The asplenic state associated with sickle cell anemia renders the patient susceptible to infections by encapsulated bacteria, especially Streptococcus pneumoniae.
